en.title: Segmented Sorting of Flower Sticks
en.description:
Sort the first K flower sticks (in input order) by length ascending, sort the remaining sticks by length descending, then concatenate the two parts. The 11 in the statement's example output does not match the input values; under the explicit rule it should be 5.

The main body of the original problem is clear, but its constraints were corrupted by OCR; this site adds n and the value ranges, and fixes obvious typos in the example.

Source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/hsbc#1-arrange-flower-sticks (pinned statement fingerprint 202828234228ff5cb0a8c031b73eb1b597d94aa826375ba5e422f5233f41012e). The input/output protocol and bounds added by this site are as described in the statement and are not claimed to be the original site's rules.
en.input: The first line contains n (0≤n≤200000); the second line contains n integers; the third line contains K (0≤K≤n). Length values are 32-bit signed integers.
en.output: Output the n lengths after concatenation according to the rule.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the full approach, proof and complexity.
hints: Split the array at K, sort each part, and concatenate them in the specified directions.
